question.text: STT (Securities Transaction Tax) is applicable on:

explanation.text: The Logic: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) under the Finance Act 2004 is levied on transactions in specified securities on a recognised stock exchange — notably exchange-traded equity and equity index derivatives (futures and options). It is not levied on exchange-traded interest rate derivatives, OTC interest rate swaps, or government securities trading on NDS-OM. The keyed option captures the only category among those listed where STT is currently chargeable. The Trap: Many candidates assume STT applies to all exchange-traded derivatives. It specifically applies to equity and equity-index derivatives, not to interest rate or currency derivatives. OTC IRS transactions are outside the STT net entirely, and NDS-OM is a debt segment on which STT does not apply. Note: The Series IV (Interest Rate Derivatives) workbook expressly states that STT is currently not applicable for ETIRD transactions but does not, on the cited pages, restate the positive rule that STT applies on exchange-traded equity derivatives. That positive rule is general securities-market knowledge drawn from the STT statute and other NISM series rather than from the Series IV pages checked.
